deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (previous page, folio 250r). Riemann sets up isotropic linear elasticity in terms of the principal dilatations λ1, λ2, λ3. P is the work of the internal forces, so P = -(energy):

δP = -∫ϱ dV Σ_i (aλ_i + bΣ_{j≠i}λ_j) δλ_i, with a > b > 0.

Equivalently the energy density is 2W = (a-b)Σλ_i² + b(Σλ_i)². In Lamé constants, a = λ+2μ and b = λ. He then writes 4W in displacement derivatives and introduces complex transverse coordinates p = y+iz for a body with axis x, i.e. a cylinder or rod.

THIS PAGE (top; the lower 2/3 is faint, largely inverted scratch work).

(1) Heading, underlined and partly crossed out; probably 'Extension' or a similar word. Case: simple extension of a circular rod of radius R and length l, density Δ.
- Assumed homogeneous strain: axial dilatation p, both transverse dilatations equal to s = q+m.
- Then 2W = ap² + 4bps + 2(a+b)s², so δW = δp(ap + 2bs) + δs(2bp + 2(a+b)s).
- Multiplying by the volume πR²l and density Δ gives the line on the page:
  4δP/(πΔR²l) = δp(ap + 2b(q+m)) + δq(2bp + 2(a+b)(q+m)).
- [Implicit step, mine] The lateral surface is free, so the coefficient of δq must vanish: s = q+m = -bp/(a+b).
- Substituting into the δp coefficient: ap - 2b²p/(a+b) = p(a² + ab - 2b²)/(a+b). The page has exactly this:
  = p δp (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b).
- So (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b) is the stretching (Young's) modulus. In Lamé form it equals μ(3λ+2μ)/(λ+μ). The transverse contraction ratio is b/(a+b) = λ/(2(λ+μ)) (Poisson's ratio).
- Marginal fragments near this line seem to be the same elimination written with other symbols.

(2) Heading 'Torsion'. The rod is twisted at rate m (angle per unit length) together with axial dilatation p and transverse dilatation q.
- The shear strain at radius r is γ = m r. By the previous page, 4W contains (a-b)γ², i.e. shear modulus μ = (a-b)/2.
- Averaging over the cross-section: (1/πR²)∫_0^R (a-b)m²r²·2πr dr = (a-b)m²R²/2.
- Adding the extension part 4W = 2ap² + 8bpq + 4(a+b)q², varying, and halving gives the page's line:
  -4δP/(2πΔR²l) = ½R²(a-b) m δm + 2δp(ap + 2bq) + 4δq((a+b)q + bp).
- At this (quadratic) order torsion decouples from p and q.
- The m-term is the classical torsional rigidity of a circular shaft, C = μπR⁴/2 = (a-b)πR⁴/4.
- Below this are two inequality lines between combinations of p and q (fragmentary; probably bounds on the ratio of contraction to extension, since a > b > 0 gives 0 < b/(a+b) < 1/2).

Purpose: comparing torsion and extension of a wire gives the two elastic constants a and b separately. This was the open experimental question of the 1840s–50s: Poisson/Navier one-constant theory (a = 3b, ratio 1/4) versus Wertheim's measurements. It also fits Riemann's 1853–54 involvement with Weber's and Kohlrausch's work on torsion of wires and elastic after-effect.

(3) The rest of the page is inverted and very faint. Visible pieces include:
- expressions with log and log log, sums of terms like p^n/(1-p^n);
- integrals of the type ∫_0^∞ e^{-x} x^{s-1}(1-e^{-x})/x dx;
- the symbol Σ, and series in p.
These look like unrelated analytic scratch work (Gamma-function or Frullani-type integrals, q-series or Lambert-type sums). They are too illegible to reconstruct reliably.
errors: Normalization of line 1: with the δP of the previous page, the left side should be -δP/(πΔR²l) (or -4δP/(4πΔR²l)). As written, '4δP/(πΔR²l)' is off by a factor of 4 and a sign relative to the Torsion line, which is exactly correct. This is either a slip or a misreading of a crossed-out numeral.
Previous page (not this one): in the displacement form of 4P, the term '2[(∂u/∂x)² ...]' must carry the factor (a-b), i.e. 2(a-b)Σ(∂u_i/∂x_i)². The transcription (or Riemann) omits it.
The free-surface condition (δq coefficient = 0) used to reach p δp (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b) is not written, but the result is correct.

results.what: Effective stretching modulus of an isotropic rod with free lateral surface: (a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b), with transverse contraction ratio b/(a+b)
results.modern_name: Young's modulus E = μ(3λ+2μ)/(λ+μ) and Poisson's ratio ν = λ/(2(λ+μ))
results.usually_credited_to: Navier/Poisson/Cauchy (1820s), Lamé & Clapeyron (1831), Lamé 1852 Leçons; Young (1807) for the modulus

results.what: Energy of a twisted circular rod: ½R²(a-b) m δm per unit cross-section, i.e. torsional rigidity μπR⁴/2
results.modern_name: Coulomb torsion law / torsional rigidity of a circular shaft (special case of Saint-Venant torsion)

results.what: Isotropic quadratic strain energy in principal dilatations with two constants a > b > 0

deep.surprise_reason: Standard textbook elasticity of the time, correctly worked: Young's modulus from Lamé constants and the torsional rigidity of a circular wire. Its only interest is biographical, as evidence of Riemann's 1853–54 engagement with Weber/Kohlrausch-style torsion experiments and the one- versus two-constant controversy. The faint analytic scratch work is unreadable and cannot support any claim.

checkable.asserts: Factorization used in the extension result
Eliminating the transverse dilatation via the free-surface condition gives p(a-b)(a+2b)/(a+b)
Riemann's modulus equals Young's modulus in Lamé constants
Transverse contraction ratio equals Poisson's ratio
Cross-section average of the torsional part of 4W
Coefficients of δm, δp, δq in the Torsion line (all three should be 0)
2W for axial dilatation p and equal transverse dilatations q

transcription_corrections: The first line has an underlined heading (top left, partly struck through), probably 'Extension' or a similar word, followed by crossed-out fragments. The '[?]' should note this heading.
The '4' in the numerator of the first equation is uncertain; the left numeral appears overwritten.
Below the second equation there are uninterpreted fragments in the denominator region (near '(a+b)'). They look like the elimination q+m = -bp/(a+b) written in other symbols.
Below the Torsion equation there are two inequality lines (with '>' and '<') relating combinations of p and q. These are not transcribed.

The lower part of the page is largely written upside down. It contains Σ, log and log log expressions, sums of terms like p^n/(1-p^n), and integrals of the type ∫_0^∞ e^{-x} x^{s-1}(1-e^{-x})/x dx. The transcription's description is reasonable but these are only partially legible.
